correctness.rationale: An isolated chord partitions the remaining endpoints into independent uniformly paired even arcs, yielding the exact probability w_{n,r} and conditional crossing mean [binom(r,2)+binom(s,2)]/3. The unconditional mean is binom(n,2)/3. Symmetry of the endpoint-gap multiplicities gives the exact negative covariance sums. The r=0 and r=n-1 cases are exactly the simple chords; r=1 and r=n-2 give the rare-event leading order. A decreasing-ratio/geometric-tail bound proves all remainder estimates; n=2 and n=3 are included in the exact formulas. An independent exact-rational enumerator checked every matching for n=2,...,7 (146598 diagrams). Enumeration is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact negative mixed covariance for all isolated chords, and specifically the limit -1/3 for the covariance contributed by exceptional nonsimple isolated chords, is not a restatement of the inspected marginal laws. The source paper first posted in 2015 studies chord-degree distributions and monolith formation; a later primary text gives crossing/top-chord generating functions on connected and indecomposable classes, and other investigated texts give independent marginal approximation rates. Other mathematical results considered concern endpoint-span/crossing covariance and long-chord point processes, not the zero-crossing event. This is a literature-based best-knowledge assessment, not a proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The simultaneous dependence of graph edge count (crossings) and isolated-vertex count in a random intersection graph is a natural mixed second-order invariant. The sharp constant -1/3 for nonsimple isolates shows that O(1/n) expected exceptional configurations leave a nonzero influence on covariance; merely replacing isolated chords by simple chords, though asymptotically correct in probability, loses the constant term -1/3. This motivates care in joint Poisson/normal moment estimates and is a structural boundary for a natural approximation, not a parameter-renamed textbook deduction.
